reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, wide-packet re-review batch 6, 2026-08-01

samples_reviewed.question_text: A rectangle is covered edge-to-edge with unit square tiles, arranged in 22 rows and 5 columns. Estimate how many unit tiles cover the rectangle in all.
A rectangle is covered edge-to-edge with unit square tiles, arranged in 3 rows and 11 columns. Estimate how many unit tiles cover the rectangle in all.
A rectangle is covered edge-to-edge with unit square tiles, arranged in 15 rows and 18 columns. Estimate how many unit tiles cover the rectangle in all.
A rectangle is covered edge-to-edge with unit square tiles, arranged in 10 rows and 15 columns. Estimate how many unit tiles cover the rectangle in all.
A rectangle is covered edge-to-edge with unit square tiles, arranged in 4 rows and 14 columns. Estimate how many unit tiles cover the rectangle in all.
A rectangle is covered edge-to-edge with unit square tiles, arranged in 17 rows and 10 columns. Estimate how many unit tiles cover the rectangle in all.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: All six samples ask the student to estimate a tile count from a stated row-by-column arrangement, e.g. seed 44's 'arranged in 15 rows and 18 columns', which matches 'estimate the area... using square tile units' directly.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The competency names 'a square OR rectangle', but every one of the six row/column pairs (22x5, 3x11, 15x18, 10x15, 4x14, 17x10) has unequal rows and columns; no sample ever illustrates a square case where rows equal columns.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Counting/estimating tiles via a rows-times-columns arrangement, up to 15x18=270 in seed 44, fits grade-3 quarter-1 reasoning about tiling ahead of formal multiplication-fact fluency.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: All six samples reuse one sentence template, 'A rectangle is covered edge-to-edge with unit square tiles, arranged in R rows and C columns...', with only the numbers changing; no alternate framing such as a word problem or a square case appears anywhere.

competency_alignment.rationale: The row/column magnitude changes across seeds, from 3x11 up to 22x5, directly build the tile-estimation skill the competency targets.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Seed 42's 22 rows by 5 columns (110 tiles) is a large grid to visually tile-count at first exposure in quarter 1, pushing toward the high end of what an early 'illustrate... using square tile units' estimation task should use.
